preparation: blood-stage, stage V gametocyte, male gamete activation, ookinete maturation, and ookinete-to-oocyst transition assays

host_control_or_selectivity: acetone/DMSO vehicle controls and stage-matched parasite assays
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: non-Artemisia purified-STL comparator; cytotoxicity and stage activity do not establish Artemisia occurrence, clinical safety, or a protein target

assay_stage: rodent/malaria assay context as reported by the indexed study
endpoint: relative antimalarial activity and combination enhancement
dose_or_ic50: April samples showed higher reported activity despite lower artemisinin than May/June; seven candidate enhancers were identified and compounds 69 and 90 were reported to potentiate artemisinin
host_control_or_selectivity: artemisinin comparison and seasonal sample contrasts
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: co-metabolite enhancement hypothesis; compound identities and matched dose/parasite-stage details require full-text extraction, and the result is not proof of terpene-only synergy

parasite: Plasmodium yoelii and A. annua extract fractions

host_control_or_selectivity: artemisinin-containing and artemisinin-reduced extract comparisons
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: candidate-metabolite and fractionation result; dose-matched constituent causality, direct target engagement, and clinical translation remain unresolved

material: herbal teas prepared from Benin and French A. annua material
preparation: LC-MS artemisinin quantification, LC-HRMS metabolomics, and isotopic microtest
endpoint: tea composition, artemisinin concentration, and IC50 association
dose_or_ic50: tea artemisinin 0.3-15.7 mg/L; artemisinin content correlated positively with activity, but tea-equivalent IC50 comparisons implicated enhancing or limiting co-metabolites; storage losses of 33%, 48%, and 24% were reported for three Benin locations
host_control_or_selectivity: pure artemisinin comparison and multiple-origin/storage contrasts
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: origin- and storage-dependent tea phenotype; unknown alkaloid features and other matrix components remain unassigned, and this is not clinical efficacy or terpene-specific attribution

material: purified annuanines A and B (cadinapyridine sesquiterpene alkaloids) and fabianine
preparation: 650 g voucher-linked Beninese leaves and stems were basified, extracted with boiling chloroform, acid/base partitioned, and fractionated by silica, MPLC, and semi-preparative HPLC; annuanine A structure was confirmed by X-ray diffraction
assay_stage: chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum FcB1 plus Caco-2, VERO, and Thp1 cell-growth assays
dose_or_ic50: annuanines A and B were inactive against P. falciparum FcB1 (IC50 >427 micromolar) and showed no notable activity in the tested healthy/cancer cell models; artemisinin, chloroquine, and doxorubicin controls were used
host_control_or_selectivity: Caco-2, VERO, and Thp1 cell controls provided a limited selectivity context; no in-vivo efficacy, pharmacokinetics, or human safety endpoint was tested
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: defined-compound negative result; annuanine B tracked a storage-associated tea feature but its correlation with activity was likely driven by artemisinin, and proposed degradation origin remains unproven

material: n-hexane extract and bio-guided C1F5/C2F5 fractions containing a 63:37 mixture of 3'-demethoxy-6-O-demethylisoguaiacin and norisoguaiacin
preparation: pre-flowering leaves and stems; voucher FES-C UNAM 11967; three solvent macerates followed by silica-gel fractionation; NMR and mass spectrometry assigned the active fraction
dose_or_ic50: n-hexane extract caused 80 +/- 9% mortality at 4 mg/mL and 68 +/- 7% at 2 mg/mL; C1F5 caused 100% at 2 mg/mL; C2F5 caused 100% at 1 mg/mL and was the structurally analyzed active subfraction
host_control_or_selectivity: distilled-water negative control and ivermectin positive control; no mammalian selectivity, infected-host, pharmacokinetic, or residue endpoint
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: defined-mixture non-terpene result; the paper infers cooperation of the two lignans but did not test purified individual standards or direct parasite-protein engagement

material: purified artemisinin; A. annua aqueous and ethanolic extracts and essential oil; A. absinthium ethanolic extract
preparation: female Mongolian gerbils received 600 exsheathed L3 by oral gavage; extracts were prepared from 45 degrees C oven-dried leaves, including 70% aqueous ethanol maceration, a boiled aqueous extract, and a commercial essential oil; treatments were delivered orally on days 4-8 post-infection

dose_or_ic50: No significant treatment effect was detected. Artemisinin burdens were 72.6 larvae after 400 mg/kg once and 78.2 after 200 mg/kg daily versus 57.0 and 58.9 in vehicle and water controls (P=0.14), corresponding to -25.2% and -34.8% reductions. A. annua ethanolic and aqueous extracts at 600 mg/kg produced 24.7% and 2.1% reductions without significance; at 1,000 mg/kg A. annua ethanolic extract, 300 mg/kg A. annua essential oil, and 1,000 mg/kg A. absinthium ethanolic extract produced 1.1%, 1.3%, and -14.9% reductions, respectively.
host_control_or_selectivity: Water, DMSO/olive oil, 3% Tween 80, and blinded parasite enumeration controls were used with n=10 per group; no signs of toxicity were observed, but no Labrasol-only group, blood-level PK, mammalian selectivity panel, or longer host follow-up was included
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: full-text negative in-vivo result at tested exposures; no extract terpene fingerprint or protein target was established. The authors discuss bioavailability, insufficient contact time, parasite redox defenses, and the gerbil model's larval-stage and host-physiology limitations; this does not negate positive ovine A. absinthium studies or establish failure of all wormwood preparations

parasite: Haemonchus contortus and ovine gastrointestinal nematodes
material: sun-dried top-third A. annua leaf material fed as whole plant
preparation: 24 male Santa Ines sheep (approximately 20 kg) were artificially infected with H. contortus and randomized to untreated control, levamisole 10 mg/kg, or A. annua at 0.2% or 0.4% body weight for 30 days; EPG was followed from day -3 through day 28
assay_stage: artificially infected Santa Ines sheep; H. contortus isolate; repeated oral whole-plant feeding
dose_or_ic50: The plant material contained 0.96% artemisinin by HPLC-IR (approximately 384 or 768 mg/day, equivalent to 19.2 or 38.4 mg/kg/day at the reported plant intakes). Mean efficacy was 32.9% at 0.2% body weight and 14.8% at 0.4%, with 47.1% and 25.2% around day 21; log-transformed EPG reductions were not significant. Levamisole averaged 89% efficacy. Sheep did not fully consume the highest dose because of bitterness.
host_control_or_selectivity: Untreated and levamisole controls, randomized six-animal groups, artificial infection, repeated EPG measurements, and animal-care oversight were reported; no adverse reactions were observed in animals that consumed the plant, but no mammalian selectivity panel, residue study, or systemic PK was included
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: quantified artemisinin plus whole-plant feeding provides a preparation- and dose-specific moderate signal, but no individual terpene or sesquiterpene lactone was assigned as causal and the absence of significant EPG reduction limits anthelmintic translation; this result should be read with the earlier negative single-dose sheep and gerbil studies

preparation: triplicate six-well-plate exposure of live adult worms recovered from sheep and goats at a local abattoir; concentrations were varied but not recoverable from the indexed full-text abstract
dose_or_ic50: Artemisinin from A. absinthium did not affect time-to-death at the tested concentrations. Allicin had a mean time-to-death of 2.15 +/- 0.58 h versus 1.00 +/- 0.58 h for fenbendazole (P=0.15), while pumpkin-seed oil reduced time-to-death to 4.15 +/- 0.73 h versus 10.00 +/- 0.73 h for saline (P<0.01).
host_control_or_selectivity: fenbendazole positive control and physiological-saline negative control; triplicate wells, but no mammalian selectivity, residue, PK, or infected-host endpoint
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: defined-compound negative adult-worm result for artemisinin attributed to A. absinthium origin; source is a conference abstract and does not establish failure of crude wormwood extracts, other chemotypes, other life stages, or in-vivo efficacy

parasite: mixed gastrointestinal nematodes in naturally infected sheep
preparation: oral whole-powder administration at 1, 2, or 3 g/kg body weight; 50 naturally infected sheep with EPG >150 randomized to three plant-dose groups, fenbendazole 5 mg/kg, or untreated infected control; fecal egg counts followed on days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, and 21
assay_stage: in vivo naturally infected ovine gastrointestinal nematodes; coproculture identified Haemonchus spp. as predominant genus
dose_or_ic50: A. maritima produced dose- and time-dependent effects, with maximum FECR 70.40% at 3 g/kg on day 21 versus 85.81% for fenbendazole; treated sheep showed improved hemoglobin, packed cell volume, and erythrocyte counts while untreated controls developed progressive anemia/leukocytosis
host_control_or_selectivity: untreated infected control, fenbendazole comparator, randomized five-group design, repeated FECR and hematology; no terpene/STL profile, residue, PK, or controlled single-parasite burden endpoint
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: abstract-level related-species whole-powder veterinary phenotype; no constituent attribution or transfer to A. absinthium, and mixed natural infection plus absent chemical standardization limit translational inference

material: 99% synthetic artemisinin and petroleum-ether A. annua leaf extract
preparation: Leaves from BALITTRO, Lembang, were room-dried for one week; 300 g powder was macerated in 3 L petroleum ether, filtered and evaporated. Thirty-five Cobb broilers were infected orally with 2000 sporulated oocysts and treated once daily for 8 days with 8.5, 17, or 34 ppm synthetic artemisinin, 17 ppm leaf extract, or sulfadiazine 200 mg
assay_stage: experimental chicken coccidiosis; seven groups of five birds with uninfected and infected untreated controls
endpoint: oocyst-excretion inhibition, cecal-lesion score, body-weight gain, packed-cell volume, and hemoglobin
dose_or_ic50: The 17 ppm A. annua leaf extract reduced oocyst excretion by 74.18%; 34 ppm synthetic artemisinin reduced it by 58.14% and sulfadiazine by 50.00%. Extract and artemisinin significantly reduced cecal lesions and maintained PCV, while body-weight gain and hemoglobin were not significantly different
host_control_or_selectivity: uninfected, infected untreated, three artemisinin doses, leaf-extract, and sulfadiazine groups; no terpene-resolved extract profile, mammalian selectivity, residue, PK, or direct parasite-protein assay
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: full-text low-dose veterinary coccidiosis comparison; petroleum-ether extract activity cannot be assigned to artemisinin or another terpene, and the study does not establish human efficacy or direct Eimeria target engagement

material: n-hexane extract of pre-flowering leaves and stems

dose_or_ic50: A. cina alone reduced infective larvae in fecal cultures by 89.9%; EPG means ranged from 25 at day -15 to 875 at day +15 and 533 at day +30; the combined D. flagrans/A. cina arm did not improve EPG and was numerically higher around postpartum

mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: full-text in-vivo related-species phenotype; no terpene/STL attribution, no direct parasite-protein target, and no transfer to A. absinthium; combined-arm interpretation remains unresolved

material: crude aqueous extract of shoots (leaves and stems)
preparation: Shoots were soaked in distilled water for 24 hours; crude aqueous extract was delivered in drinking water at 0.4 g/kg body weight for three consecutive days beginning 25 days after infection. The study used 180 male turkey poults across three repeated experiments, with 500 embryonated eggs used for infection

endpoint: fecal egg count, worm burden, growth performance, biochemical measures, and liver histopathology
dose_or_ic50: At seven days after treatment, the extract group showed 97.78% fecal-egg-count reduction and 96.07% worm-count reduction, compared with 97.31% and 95.08% for albendazole at 20 mg/kg; extract-treated birds had improved growth measures and no reported liver lesions in the examined sections
host_control_or_selectivity: uninfected and infected untreated controls, albendazole comparator, three repeated experiments, n=15 per group per experiment with n=12 for fecal-egg analysis and n=5 for worm burden/biochemistry; no terpene-resolved chemistry, residue, PK, or mammalian selectivity
mechanistic_or_translation_boundary: full-text poultry vermifuge phenotype with a crude aqueous preparation; the high reported efficacy is host-, parasite-, dose-, and preparation-specific and cannot be assigned to thujone, santonin, or another terpene/STL or transferred to human use
